result.summary: Independently re-verified TEST-DESIGNER's rework claim from scratch, not accepted on trust. (1) Read test/letflow/definitions/store_test.exs lines 758-940 (the rewritten 'Regression -- activate/2 cross-row TOCTOU' describe block) directly and traced the mechanism against lib/letflow/definitions.ex's actual query sequence (run_activate_transaction/4, activate_draft/2): step 1 SELECT...FOR UPDATE (per-row lock, no cross-row contention), step 2 deprecate-step UPDATE (WHERE name=^name AND status='active'), step 3 self-activate UPDATE (WHERE id=^id AND status='draft'). The telemetry handler counts process_definitions-sourced [:letflow, :repo, :query] events per-process via the process dictionary (correctly isolated, since :telemetry.execute runs synchronously in the emitting process, not a separate logger process -- confirmed myself by reading deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql.ex lines 1271-1316's log/5, which is invoked as DBConnection's :log callback in the calling process immediately after each query completes and before the caller's code proceeds) and blocks via a plain receive on the 2nd such event per task -- i.e. exactly after step 2 completes and before step 3 is issued. Handler attachment happens strictly before either task is released past its own :toctou_run gate, so there is no register-vs-fire race. Traced the actual Postgres semantics of the forced window: both self-activate UPDATEs (step 3) target different rows but the same uq_active_definition partial-unique-index key; Postgres makes the second (loser) UPDATE block server-side on the first (winner)'s uncommitted index entry, then raises a real unique_violation once the winner commits -- which propagates as a raised exception out of Repo.transaction and is caught by activate/2's own try/rescue, converting to {:error, {:transaction_failed, exception}} exactly as asserted. No gap found -- this is a sound, not merely lucky, forcing mechanism. (2) Confirmed via `git show --stat ba676cf` that the rework commit touched only test/letflow/definitions/store_test.exs and test/specs/REQ-030.md -- lib/letflow/definitions.ex is absent from the commit, and `git diff f3ee92c ba676cf -- test/letflow/definitions/store_test.exs` shows exactly one hunk (lines 758+), confirming no other test case (AC1-AC9, all 9 forbidden-transition cells, AC2 concurrency) was touched by this rework. (3) Independently ran the isolated file (test/letflow/definitions/store_test.exs, 27 tests) 6 times across 6 fresh seeds never used by TEST-DESIGNER (31337, 900123, 55501, 2026081, 610, 848484): all 6 report 'Result: 27 passed', 0 failures -- the TOCTOU test's own assertions (exactly one success, exactly one {:error, {:transaction_failed, _}}, count_active_by_name==1) held on every run, not just some. For seed 848484 I captured the full debug query log directly (not the test's own report) and independently grepped it myself: exactly one 'QUERY ERROR' in the entire 27-test run, on the exact self-activate UPDATE statement (`WHERE ((p0."id" = $3) AND (p0."status" = 'draft'))`) -- a real Postgres-level failure at precisely the targeted window, corroborating the mechanism independent of trusting the assertion alone. (4) Re-read test/specs/REQ-030.md's rewritten Regression section end-to-end: it now states the mechanism (telemetry rendezvous, why service_scope_validator and a new test-only hook were both rejected as the pause point) and cites this run's own reproduction evidence rather than an unverified claim -- matches what I independently observed, no overclaiming found, the prior MAJOR issue's root cause is also honestly named in both the spec and the test file's own comments. (5) Ran the full test/letflow/definitions/store_test.exs + test/letflow/definitions_test.exs suite twice more with fresh seeds (424242, 99887): both report 'Result: 40 passed', 0 failures, matching the pre-rework baseline exactly, no count change. (6) Light regression pass on everything checked in the original (non-reworked) PASS-track items: grepped both files for TODO/@tag :skip/@tag :pending (zero hits), confirmed 27 top-level `test` blocks still present in store_test.exs (matches the 27-passed count, nothing silently dropped), grepped for hardcoded secrets/connection strings (zero hits) -- all consistent with no regression outside the single targeted describe block.
